The instant CRMP filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C seeks quashment of FIR bearing Crime No. 0356/2019, P.S. Rajendra Nagar, Raipur dated 14/10/2019 registered against the applicants for the offences under Section 384/34 of the IPC, on the ground of false implication.

sentences.text: At the very outset, learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the FIR lodged by the present applicants against the Complainant for the offence punishable under Section 376 & 354 of the IPC, a closure report has been filed, however, the same has not been accepted.
So far as present FIR is concerned, it has been lodged just after three weeks of the FIR lodged by the applicants against the Complainant to counter the same.
He would submit that in the present case, the Investigation Officer is yet to file closure report.
3. Per Contra, learned counsel for the State, though does not oppose the fact regarding lodging of FIR against the complainant, submits that investigation is going on.
4. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.

5. Having considered the rival submissions made by the counsel for the parties and the fact that there are counter FIRs against each other, this Court is of the opinion to direct the concerned Investigating Officer to conclude the investigation and submit the report under Section 173 (3) of the Cr.P.C in respect of the subject FIR within a period of 6 weeks.
6. Accordingly, the Cr.M.P is disposed of with the aforesaid directions.
However, the interim order granted earlier vide order dated 19/12/2019 shall remain operative and the applicants shall not be arrested for a period of six weeks.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Bibhu Datta Guru) (Ramesh Sinha)
